¿Cómo se nombra un compuesto orgánico?: How do you name an organic compound?
Se elige el grupo principal (ácido > ést: The principal group is chosen (acid > ester > amide > nitrile > aldehyde > ketone > alcohol > amine), the chain with the most principal groups, multiple bonds and carbons, and it is numbered to give the lowest locants. CH₃–CH(OH)–CH₃ is propan-2-ol and CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH₃ is 2-methylpropane.
¿Cómo se nombra un ciclo o un derivado d: How do you name a ring or a benzene derivative?
Se antepone «ciclo» al alcano: C₆H₁₂ es: “cyclo” is put before the alkane: C₆H₁₂ is cyclohexane. The ring is numbered giving 1 to the principal group (cyclohexanol) or, if there is none, to a carbon of the double bond and then to the substituents with the lowest locants: 1,2-dimethylcyclohexane. If the ring has as many carbons as the chain or more, it is the parent; if not, it becomes a substituent (cyclohexyl). From benzene, toluene, phenol, aniline and benzoic acid are accepted, and with two substituents we speak of ortho (1,2), meta (1,3) and p- (1,4): 1,4-dimethylbenzene is p-xylene.
¿Qué es el cis y el trans en un anillo?: What are cis and trans in a ring?
En un anillo no se puede girar, así que: In a ring there is no rotation, so two substituents can lie on the same side of the plane (cis) or on opposite sides (trans). 1,2-Dimethylcyclohexane has three stereoisomers: the cis, which is a meso form (a plane of symmetry, achiral), and the trans, which forms a pair of enantiomers (1R,2R) and (1S,2S).
¿Cómo se sabe si un centro es R o S, o u: How do you know whether a center is R or S, or a double bond E or Z?
Con las reglas de Cahn-Ingold-Prelog: se: With the Cahn-Ingold-Prelog rules: the substituents are ranked by atomic number. With the lowest priority one at the back, if the other three turn clockwise it is R and if they turn counterclockwise, S. In a double bond, if the highest-priority ones are on the same side it is Z and if not, E. With n chiral centers there are at most 2ⁿ stereoisomers.

Como en clase: grupos CH3, CH2, CH, OH,: As in class: CH3, CH2, CH, OH, NH2… groups joined with -, = or # (or ≡), and branches in parentheses: CH3-CH(OH)-CH3. The abbreviations COOH, CHO, CONH2 and CN are accepted. Rings are written in SMILES.
Se escribe en <b>SMILES</b>: cada letra: It is written in SMILES: each letter is an atom (C, N, O, S, F, Cl, Br, I) and hydrogens are added automatically. = and # are the double and triple bond; branches go in parentheses: CC(C)C is 2-methylpropane, CC(=O)O is ethanoic acid. For chirality use [C@H] or [C@@H] (seen from the first neighbor, the other three go counterclockwise or clockwise) and for E/Z, the marks / and \: C/C=C/C is trans (E), C/C=C\C is cis (Z). Rings are closed with a number: C1CCCCC1 is cyclohexane and benzene is written with a lowercase "c", c1ccccc1 (Cc1ccccc1 is toluene). In a ring, [C@H] and [C@@H] tell whether the substituent is above or below the plane: C[C@H]1CCCC[C@H]1C is cis-1,2-dimethylcyclohexane.

<b>Grupo principal.</b> Manda el de más: Principal group. The one with the highest priority rules: carboxylic acid > ester > amide > nitrile > aldehyde > ketone > alcohol > thiol > amine. The other groups become prefixes (hydroxy, oxo, amino, halogens…).
<b>Cadena principal.</b> La que contiene: Main chain. The one containing the most principal groups; if tied, the one with the most double and triple bonds and, after that, the one with the most carbons.
<b>Numeración.</b> Por el extremo que da: Numbering. From the end that gives the lowest locants: first to the principal group, then to the multiple bonds and finally to the substituents (and, if still tied, to the one that comes first alphabetically).
<b>Nombre.</b> Sustituyentes en orden al: Name. Substituents in alphabetical order (not counting di-, tri-…), the chain with its "an", "en" or "yn" and the suffix of the principal group: 3-ethyl-2-methylpentane, but-3-en-2-ol, 3-methylbutanoic acid.
<b>Anillo o cadena.</b> Es el compuesto: Ring or chain. The parent compound is the one with more principal groups; if tied, the ring when it has as many carbons as the longest chain or more: methylcyclohexane, but 1-cyclopropylheptane. If the parent is the chain, the ring becomes a substituent (cyclohexyl, phenyl).
<b>Numeración del anillo.</b> El 1 es el: Ring numbering. Number 1 is the atom with the principal group (cyclohexanol, cyclohexanecarboxylic acid); if there is none, a carbon of the double bond (3-methylcyclohexene) and, after that, the lowest locants for the substituents: 1,2-dimethylcyclohexane.
<b>Benceno.</b> Con un solo sustituyente: Benzene. With a single substituent no locant is needed (ethylbenzene). The names toluene, phenol, aniline, benzaldehyde and benzoic acid are accepted, and with two substituents we speak of ortho (1,2), meta (1,3) and p- (1,4), although the IUPAC name uses the numbers.
<b>Cis y trans.</b> En un anillo, dos su: Cis and trans. In a ring, two substituents on the same side of the plane are cis and on opposite sides, trans. 1,2-Dimethylcyclohexane has three stereoisomers: the cis (meso form) and the two enantiomers of the trans.
Se ordenan los sustituyentes de un carbo: The substituents of a carbon are ranked by the atomic number of the atom attached to it; if tied, the set of atoms in the next sphere is compared, and so on until the tie is broken. A double bond counts as two single bonds (the atom at the other end is duplicated).
<b>Centro quiral</b> (carbono con cuatro: Chiral center (carbon with four different substituents): look with the lowest-priority substituent in the back; if the other three, from highest to lowest, turn clockwise it is R (rectus) and if they turn counterclockwise, S (sinister).
<b>Doble enlace</b> con dos sustituyente: Double bond with two different substituents on each carbon: if the highest-priority ones are on the same side it is Z (zusammen) and if they are on opposite sides, E (entgegen).
Con <i>n</i> centros quirales (y dobles: With n chiral centers (and E/Z double bonds) there are at most 2n stereoisomers; if the molecule has a plane of symmetry there are fewer, because meso forms appear (achiral, even though they have chiral centers).
<b>Constitucional o estructural.</b> Mis: Constitutional or structural. Same molecular formula, different connection of atoms. Chain (butane and isobutane), position (propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol) and function (ethanol and methoxyethane).
<b>Estereoisomería.</b> Mismo orden de e: Stereoisomerism. Same order of bonds, different arrangement in space. Geometric (cis/trans, E/Z) and optical: enantiomers are non-superimposable mirror images and rotate the plane of polarized light in opposite directions; diastereomers are not mirror images.
Más de un anillo en la misma molécula (b: More than one ring in the same molecule (bicyclics, spiro, naphthalene, biphenyl), heterocycles (oxirane, pyridine, furan), secondary and tertiary amines, N-substituted amides, acid halides and substituents with an acyl group.
Moléculas de C, H, N, O, F, S, Cl, Br e: Molecules of C, H, N, O, F, S, Cl, Br and I with chains and, at most, one ring (cycloalkanes, cycloalkenes or benzene), written in SMILES; the condensed formula is only for chains. Two or more rings (bicyclics, naphthalene, biphenyl), heterocycles and other elements are rejected or not named, with a warning.
En un anillo con dos o más sustituyentes: In a ring with two or more substituents the cis/trans is taken from the @ and @@ of the SMILES (with centers on both), not from a drawing; "-ylidene" groups (a double bond between the ring and a chain) are not named yet.
El nombre IUPAC cubre los casos habitual: The IUPAC name covers the usual cases of chains and substituents; if the molecule goes beyond what it can name, it says so instead of making up a name.
La forma 3D es una geometría aproximada: The 3D shape is an approximate geometry to see the arrangement of the atoms, not an energy optimization.
